title: SF3116 (2017-2018 Regular): School teachers and employees permit to carry firearms in schools; active shooter firearm training

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/90/2018/0/SF/3116/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Introduced version as filed (SF 3116, 2017-2018 session). Section 2 strikes the word 'or' and a period in the exceptions list (punctuation). Section 3(b) text says a sheriff must issue a school permit to qualifying applicants unless denied under subd. 6.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 299C.26): The superintendent of the Bureau of Criminal Apprehension, in consultation with security and law enforcement experts with appropriate qualifications and experience in responding to active shooter situations, must establish a school and postsecondary institution teacher and employee firearm training program that includes at a minimum training in active shooter situations.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 609.66, subd. 1d): (10) teachers and employees of public elementary, middle, and secondary schools; charter schools under chapter 124E; and postsecondary institutions under chapter 136F or 137 who have a school permit to carry under section 624.714, subdivision 8b.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.714, subd. 8b): A teacher or other employee of a public elementary, middle, or secondary school; charter school under chapter 124E; or postsecondary institution under chapter 136F or 137 may apply to the sheriff of the county where the teacher or employee resides for a school permit to carry. A school permit to carry issued under this subdivision expires one year after the date of issue.
Section 4 (Minn. Stat. 624.714, subd. 18): This subdivision does not apply to teachers and employees authorized to carry firearms under section 609.66, subdivision 1d, paragraph (f).
